title: t3 (glassbox-bench seed-1): no behaviour to explain - the checkpoint does not compute the dataset's function
label: null finding - no mechanism
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from 6 symbols (ba, ka, ne, se, va, ve); one output symbol (D, E or M) expected at the last position.
summary: On the local-full backend (full precision) the checkpoint does not perform the behaviour. On 200 prompts its top-1 accuracy against the dataset answers is 0.055, below uniform chance over the 11-token vocabulary (0.091); the mean logit difference between the correct and an incorrect output symbol is 0.015 (std 0.28) on clean prompts and -0.020 on corrupt prompts. The sampled predictions are an input symbol ('ne'), not an output symbol. The pre-registered prediction that accuracy would be >= 0.9 was refuted. Per protocol the investigation stopped here: with no behaviour there is no circuit to localise, so no heads or MLP layers are claimed and no verification was run.

claims.text: The checkpoint does not perform the behaviour: top-1 accuracy 0.055 on 200 prompts (uniform chance over 11 tokens is 0.091), mean correct-minus-incorrect logit diff 0.015 +/- 0.28 (local-full, full precision).
The model's logit diff does not distinguish clean from corrupt prompts (0.015 vs -0.020), so there is no input-dependent signal for the answer to patch or attribute.
No attention head or MLP layer is claimed as part of a circuit; the claimed circuit is empty because there is no behaviour to implement.

limitations: Only the baseline was run (2 of 25 experiments). No component-level experiment was performed, by design: localising a circuit for a behaviour the model does not show would fit noise.
The function the model itself computes at the last position (it appears to emit an input symbol, 'ne', in the 4 sampled predictions) was not characterised; only 4 example predictions were inspected.

The task statement says the dataset answers are the model's own outputs; E0002 contradicts that for this checkpoint. Either the checkpoint or the dataset labels are not what the task statement describes. I could not determine which from inside the lab.

By hand inspection the seed-0 labels fit 'more ka than se -> M, more se than ka -> E, tie -> D' on 63 of 64 examples (E0001). This describes the labels, not this model, and was not tested by an experiment.
open_questions: Is this checkpoint an untrained / random-initialised model paired with another model's labels?
What does the checkpoint output across the full input space, and is that output input-dependent at all?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null finding - no mechanism

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The loaded checkpoint reproduces the dataset's answers (which on seed 0 fit 'compare count of ka vs count of se: more ka -> M, more se -> E, tie -> D' on 63/64 examples), so top-1 accuracy at the last position is high.

prediction.statement: The model outputs the dataset answer on at least 90% of 200 prompts
